challenge.better_approach: Considered raising 1500 to a bigger constant: it re-creates the same cliff at the next larger writes_to (cdfc is 323 files at ~17 s each, about 93 min). Considered deriving the bound from file count x proofs x 120 s: that number is the verb's own bound, already enforced per run inside hollow.py, so a second copy in the shell only adds a place to disagree. Dropping the outer bound plus a loud status is the smallest.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the hollow verb's per-run 120 s bound really covers the case of a hung run, so dropping the outer bound cannot hang prove.sh forever. hollow.py:1138 passes timeout= to each run and reports a timeout as returncode None; the builder reads that before deleting the shell bound.
challenge.prior_art: Grepped CairnCommons tickets, questions, troubles and ideas for `timeout 1500` and for a hollow being killed or timed out: the hits are 95f8c561e742, d48d54dccde6 and e038544a9b60, which quote the command as a recipe step, and 217c82fe7b57, which names build commits (unrelated). Sibling shape: 8b171277190c (sail's chart waits as long as a gate can take, proof test_a_chart_waits_as_long_as_a_gate_can_take.py). No ticket covers this.
challenge.real_collision: None real. The recipe text in 95f8 and d48d says the hollow is exactly `timeout 1500 bin/cairn test --hollow <ticket> --seal`; that is a record of how those voyages ran, not a constraint on prove.sh. Distinction recorded.

answers.falsifier: With a stub hollow exiting 124, prove.sh exits nonzero naming the hollow and its status; with a stub exiting 0 it exits 0 with the hollow's last lines; prove.sh wraps the hollow in no wall-clock bound of its own. Wrong intent if a long hollow should instead be split or sampled (then the cure is in hollow.py, not prove.sh).
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured, not imagined: /home/akien/.akien/temp/walk-cdfc928cc5ff/prove.out holds the silent hollow section of cdfc928cc5ff prove run, 2026-11-21
answers.how: In cairn/devices/cc/scripts/prove.sh drop the fixed `timeout 1500` around `bin/cairn test --hollow $ID --seal` (the verb already bounds each proof run at 120 s, hollow.py:978), and take the hollow's own status from PIPESTATUS rather than tail's: nonzero prints `HOLLOW DID NOT FINISH (exit N)` and exits 6. A red-first proof in cairn/devices/cc/proofs/ runs prove.sh's hollow step against a stub bin/cairn.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces): a killed hollow exits prove.sh 0 and prints nothing. Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass): a hollow that cannot finish leaves a ticket whose writes scale past 1500 s unprovable.
answers.what: prove.sh's hollow step runs the hollow to its end under the hollow verb's own per-run bound, and a hollow that does not finish stops prove.sh loudly with its exit status instead of exiting 0.

bullets.text: prove.sh's last line pipes the hollow through tail, so prove.sh's exit is tail's: a hollow killed at 1500 s printed nothing and the walk went on to a confirmed verdict; only the PROVED gate's hollow_evidence_absent caught it (cdfc928cc5ff, 2026-11-21).
A hollow's cost scales with writes_to x proof runtime; cdfc's 323 commons records at ~17 s per tester run is ~93 min, past any fixed shell bound picked for code tickets.

title: prove.sh's hollow step runs the hollow to its end under the hollow verb's own per-run bound, and a hollow that does not
